messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS in United Kingdom during the 1990s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: UK Data Service British Household Panel Survey 1991 2000 dataset
UK Data Service British Social Attitudes survey 1990s data catalogue
UK Data Service 1991 census samples anonymised records social class dataset
UK Data Service Family Resources Survey 1994 1999 dataset
action.query: UK Data Service British Household Panel Survey 1991 2000 dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"British Household Panel Survey (BHPS): Waves 1–18, 1991–2009","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-5151-2","justification":"One of the most comprehensive longitudinal datasets for studying social stratification in 1990s Britain. Beginning in 1991, the survey follows individuals and households over time, collecting information on income, employment, occupation, education, family structure, housing, and socioeconomic circumstances. The 1991–1999 waves are particularly useful for investigating class mobility, income inequality, occupational hierarchies, social exclusion, and differences between demographic groups."},{"title":"1991 Census: Individual Sample of Anonymised Records for Great Britain (SARs)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-7210-1","justification":"A large-scale dataset containing approximately 1.2 million individual records from the 1991 Census, representing roughly 2% of the population. Includes variables describing social class, socioeconomic status, occupation, employment, educational qualifications, ethnicity, gender, age, housing tenure, and geographical location. Particularly valuable for examining the distribution of social classes and demographic groupings across England, Scotland, and Wales at the beginning of the 1990s."},{"title":"1991 Census: Household Sample of Anonymised Records for Great Britain (SARs)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-7211-1","justification":"Provides household-level census microdata from 1991, including social class, occupation, economic activity, housing tenure, household composition, and demographic characteristics. Particularly useful for studying socioeconomic differences between households, class-based residential patterns, family structures, and relationships between social stratification and housing conditions in early-1990s Britain."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1990","url_or_doi":"https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/ICPSR/studies/3093","justification":"A nationally representative survey examining British attitudes toward economic inequality, government policies, taxation, education, racial discrimination, employment, housing, and social issues. Useful for investigating how class, ethnicity, education, and other social group characteristics relate to political and social attitudes at the beginning of the 1990s."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1996","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/3921","justification":"Provides survey data on social attitudes in Britain during 1996. Useful for investigating relationships between socioeconomic position, demographic characteristics, political preferences, and attitudes toward social institutions. Researchers can examine differences between occupational classes, educational groups, and other population categories during the middle of the decade."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1999","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/4318","justification":"Provides survey evidence on British social attitudes at the end of the 1990s. Suitable for analysing differences in attitudes across socioeconomic and demographic groups, including those defined by occupation, education, age, and gender. Can be compared with earlier British Social Attitudes surveys to investigate changes in social divisions and public opinion throughout the decade."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1998","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/4131","justification":"A late-1990s survey suitable for examining social and political attitudes across different population groups. Relevant to research on class differences, social identities, public perceptions of inequality, and relationships between demographic characteristics and social attitudes. Particularly useful alongside the 1996 and 1999 surveys for investigating changes over time."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1997","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/4072","justification":"Contains survey information relevant to studying social differences and attitudes among population groups in Britain in 1997. Researchers can use demographic and socioeconomic characteristics to investigate differences between social classes, educational groups, generations, and other categories. Provides a useful observation point during a period of significant political and social change."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1995","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/3764","justification":"Provides mid-1990s British survey data suitable for exploring social attitudes and differences across socioeconomic and demographic categories. Useful for examining how occupation, education, age, and other characteristics relate to social and political views. Can support comparative analyses of social divisions across successive survey years."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey, 1994","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/3572","justification":"A nationally focused social attitudes dataset from 1994 that can support research on social stratification, population group differences, and attitudes toward public policy. Particularly relevant for comparing perspectives across occupational, educational, and demographic categories during the early-to-middle 1990s."},{"title":"1991 Census: Individual Sample of Anonymised Records for Northern Ireland (SARs)","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/7212","justification":"Provides individual-level microdata from the 1991 Northern Ireland Census. Relevant for studying socioeconomic and demographic differences, employment, occupational characteristics, household circumstances, and population groupings in Northern Ireland. Complements the Great Britain census samples and allows researchers to examine social stratification across the wider United Kingdom."},{"title":"1991 Census: Household Sample of Anonymised Records for Northern Ireland (SARs)","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/7213","justification":"A household-level census dataset covering Northern Ireland in 1991. Useful for investigating household composition, socioeconomic circumstances, employment-related differences, housing characteristics, and demographic groupings. Can complement the corresponding Great Britain dataset when studying household-level social stratification throughout the United Kingdom."},{"title":"British Social Attitudes Survey: Cumulative Dataset, 1983–2012","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/7875","justification":"A cumulative resource bringing together multiple years of British Social Attitudes data, including observations from the 1990s. Particularly valuable for examining longer-term patterns in social attitudes and differences between population groups. Researchers can restrict analyses to the 1990–1999 period and investigate relationships between socioeconomic characteristics, demographic identities, and changing attitudes toward social and political issues."},{"title":"1970 British Cohort Study: Age 21 Sample Survey, 1992","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/1440","justification":"A longitudinal birth-cohort dataset examining individuals born in Britain in 1970 as they entered early adulthood. The 1992 survey is particularly useful for investigating educational attainment, early employment experiences, socioeconomic circumstances, and differences in young adult life trajectories. Supports research into intergenerational social mobility, educational inequality, and the reproduction of social advantage."},{"title":"1970 British Cohort Study: Age 29, Sweep 6, 1999–2000","url_or_doi":"https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/4029","justification":"A longitudinal survey following people born in Britain in 1970 into adulthood at the end of the 1990s. Relevant for studying educational and occupational pathways, socioeconomic inequalities, employment trajectories, and family circumstances. Particularly valuable when combined with earlier cohort observations to examine how childhood social background relates to adult socioeconomic position and class mobility."}]}
